title: Stratified deferred preemption with adaptive KV watermarking
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: implement a preemption policy that reduces SLO violations at the P99 tail while preserving fair GPU memory allocation and high KV cache hit rates. We will introduce a stratified deferred preemption mechanism that groups in-flight requests into quick/elastic/critical lanes and applies adaptive KV watermarks to avoid unnecessary eviction for small hot working sets. The design trades off immediate slot reclamation versus downstream latency regressions caused by KV churn.
background: Continuous batching currently uses an aggressive preemptor that reclaims kernels to satisfy high-priority requests. This leads to frequent KV cache evictions for multi-tenant workloads, increasing P95/P99 latencies for queries that rely on warmed KV state. Existing tickets addressed fairness and SLO-driven preemption, but we still see regression when tenant hotsets are small and eviction overhead is high. We need a policy that is aware of KV residency and GPU memory fragmentation patterns.
proposal_summary: 1) Classify arriving requests into three strata using existing SLA hints + runtime predictor (quick: short expected tokens, elastic: best-effort, critical: latency SLO at risk). 2) When reclaiming GPU slots, defer preemption for quick lane and low-resident KV requests with a short grace window (configurable e.g., 50-200ms). 3) Maintain per-tenant adaptive KV watermarks: low, nominal, high — watermarks shift based on access skew, eviction cost, and current GPU free memory. 4) Eviction prioritizes blocks with low reuse probability and respects tenant fairness quotas. 5) Expose metrics and canary flags to measure impact before global rollout.
tradeoffs: Deferring preemption can increase short-term queuing and reduce throughput under pathological bursts.
Adaptive watermarks reduce eviction churn but require accurate reuse estimation; misestimation can increase memory pressure.
Adding per-tenant state increases scheduler complexity and memory for bookkeeping.
Complex policy may be harder to debug in prod—need traceability and deterministic replay for postmortems.

Add per-tenant KV residency tracking + moving-average reuse score
Implement deferred preemption timer with jitter and exponential backoff for repeated deferrals
Adaptive watermark controller: feedback loop using eviction rate and tail latency signals
Eviction ranking: integrate LFU-style score + kernel residency cost
Unit + integration tests for eviction correctness and preemption/unwind paths

Dashboard: add per-tenant KV hitrate, eviction rate, preemption deferral count, P95/P99 latency

acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for critical-lane requests decreases or remains flat in 90% of replayed workloads compared to baseline preemptor
KV cache hitrate increases by >= 5% for tenants with hotsets <= 32MB in replay tests
No regression in overall system throughput > 3% in steady-state multi-tenant runs
Metrics emitted: preemption_deferrals_total, kv_watermark_level, eviction_cost_estimate, tenant_fairness_score
Canary rollout completed with two production clusters and roll-back documented
